title: Spatiotemporal-Augmented Graph Neural Networks for Human Mobility Simulation
journal: IEEE Transactions on Knowledge and Data Engineering
authors: Yu Wang; Tongya Zheng; Shunyu Liu; Zunlei Feng; Kaixuan Chen; Yunzhi Hao; Mingli Song
abstract: Human mobility patterns have shown significant applications in policy-decision scenarios and economic behavior researches. The human mobility simulation task aims to generate human mobility trajectories given a small set of trajectory data, which have aroused much concern due to the scarcity and sparsity of human mobility data. Existing methods mostly rely on the static relationships of locations, while largely neglect the dynamic spatiotemporal effects of locations. On the one hand, spatiotempora correspondences of visit distributions reveal the spatial proximity and the functionality similarity of locations. On the other hand, the varying durations in different locations hinder the iterative generation process of the mobility trajectory. Therefore, we propose a nove framework to model the dynamic spatiotemporal effects of locations, namely SpatioTemporal-Augmented gRaph neura networks (STAR). The STAR framework designs various spatiotemporal graphs to capture the spatiotemporal correspondences and builds a novel dwell branch to simulate the varying durations in locations, which is finally optimized in an adversarial manner. The comprehensive experiments over four real datasets for the human mobility simulation have verified the superiority of STAR to state-of-the-art methods. Our code is available at https://github.com/Star607/STAR-TKDE.
abstractZh: 人类移动模式在政策决策场景和经济行为研究中具有重要应用。人类移动模拟旨在根据少量轨迹数据生成移动轨迹，由于移动数据稀缺和稀疏，该任务受到广泛关注。现有方法主要依赖地点间静态关系，较少考虑地点的动态时空效应。一方面，访问分布的时空对应关系揭示地点的空间邻近性和功能相似性；另一方面，不同地点停留时长的差异给移动轨迹迭代生成带来困难。因此，我们提出时空增强图神经网络（STAR）框架，对地点动态时空效应建模。该框架设计多种时空图捕捉时空对应关系，并构建新的停留分支模拟地点停留时长差异，最终通过对抗方式优化。四个真实数据集上的综合实验表明，STAR在人类移动模拟中优于现有先进方法。代码公开于https://github.com/Star607/STAR-TKDE。
